title: QBR metrics synthesis & ops notebook — latency / cost / cache
body:
Purpose:
This is an operations-focused notebook for assembling the QBR metric definitions we report upstream. The goal is to harmonize how engineering, CS, and account execs interpret latency, availability, cost/token and cache effectiveness so QBR conversations have consistent signal.

Scope & audience:
- Audience: CS leads, SRE partners, account execs, and engineering owners for hosted and dedicated customers.
- Scope: metrics used in quarterly business reviews (QBRs) for accounts with non-trivial usage (>10k monthly tokens). Not a product roadmap doc — it’s an operational, measurement-first reference.

High-level measurement principles (ops-first):
1) One source of truth: published metric should map to a single query in the metrics warehouse (see Data sources).
2) Windowing matters: use 30d rolling for trend, 7d rolling for recent regressions, and 1d for outage analysis.
3) Percentile focus for latency (p50/p95/p99); mean is noisy for bursty traffic.
4) Signal hygiene: annotate known maintenance windows and planned degradations before computing quarterly aggregates.

Metric definitions (operational wording):
1) Latency — end-to-end request latency
- Definition: Time from request ingress at the public API edge to the final token response completion returned to the client (includes network transmission, routing, model inference, and our streaming assembly).
- Primary percentiles: p50, p95, p99 measured in milliseconds.
- Calculation: For a given window W, pX = Xth percentile of observed request latencies for successful requests (2xx). Exclude requests with server error codes and exclude client timeouts >60s (they should be investigated separately).
- Example: p95 = 420ms over 7d rolling.
- Data caveats: Distinguish between cold-start spikes (scale events) and steady-state. Tag spikes with autoscale_event_id.

2) Uptime / Availability — API availability for customer requests
- Definition: Percentage of requests that returned a successful response (2xx) within the SLA latency ceiling over the measurement window.
- SLA ceiling: default is 3s for hosted API; per-customer SLA overrides for Dedicated.
- Calculation: availability = (successful_requests_within_sla / total_valid_requests) * 100. Exclude maintenance windows documented in maintenance_log.
- Example: availability = (9,850 / 10,000) * 100 = 98.5% over 30d.

3) Cost per token (unit economics) — incremental execution cost normalized to tokens
- Definition: the allocated infra + model runtime cost divided by billed tokens for the same window. This is a blended per-token cost used in QBR economics discussions (not invoice).
- Calculation (simplified for QBR): cost/token = (GPU_runtime_cost + infra_overhead + network_egress_alloc) / total_billed_tokens. Express as USD per 1k tokens for readability.
- Example: cost/token = (6,200 USD) / (2,000,000 tokens) = 0.0031 USD/token -> 3.1 USD per 1k tokens.
- Notes: For Dedicated customers, use reserved allocation line-items; for hosted customers use modeled runtime costs from cost-sim job (cost-sim-v2). Exclude embeddings and re-ranking if charged differently — document line_items used.

4) Cache hit rate — effective reuse of KV/prefix caches
- Definition: fraction of token-generation requests where at least one cache layer avoided a full model forward (prefix or KV hit that reduced compute).
- Calculation: cache_hit_rate = cache_hits / cache_eligible_requests. Define cache_eligible_requests: requests with recognized prompt hash and model-compatible variant.
- Example: If 18,000 eligible requests and 11,700 hits -> 65% cache hit rate over 30d.
- Sub-metrics to track: prefix_hit_rate, kv_cache_reuse_rate, cold_start_fraction.
- Caveat: hits are not all equal — partial hits that save a few KV layers still valuable. Consider weighted cache savings (tokens_saved_estimate / tokens_total).

Suggested metric tags (for QBR table):
- Metric name, window, owner, data_query_id, target, recent_value, delta_vs_prev_qtr, action_trigger, notes.

Sample KPI table (text version for copy/paste into slides):
- Row format: Metric | Window | Owner | Target | Recent | Delta (vs prev qtr) | Source | Action trigger
- Latency p95 | 30d | eng-sre (Priya Rao) | < 500ms | 420ms | -10% | query:metrics.latency.p95.customerXYZ.30d | p95 > 800ms -> open incident
- Uptime | 30d | cs-ops (Maya Patel) | >= 99.5% | 98.5% | -0.7ppt | query:metrics.availability.30d.customerXYZ | <99% -> escalate to AD
- Cost /1k tokens | 30d | finance-ops (Noah Blake) | < $3.5 / 1k | $3.1 / 1k | +6% | query:billing.cost_per_token.customerXYZ.30d | >$4.5/1k -> cost review + batching recommendations
- Cache hit rate | 30d | eng-ml (Liam Chen) | >= 60% | 65% | +4ppt | query:metrics.cache.hit_rate.30d.customerXYZ | <45% -> recommend prefix caching + QA prompt patterns

QBR scoring suggestion (ops-weighted grade):
- Per-metric grade: green/amber/red based on target band.
- Weights (example): latency 35%, uptime 30%, cost 20%, cache 15%.
- QBR score = sum(metric_grade_score * weight). Map numeric score to simple summary for execs.

Runbook / Play triggers (short):
- Latency regression (p95 jump >50% vs baseline): trigger step: (1) Check autoscale events, (2) verify model variant routing, (3) raise SRE paging if p95 > 1s for >30m. Link: CON-3421 (runbook stub).
- Availability drop: (1) Check error logs, (2) confirm maintenance windows, (3) roll back last deployment if correlated.
- Cost spike: (1) Check model mix (L > S), (2) look for sudden traffic pattern changes (long sequences), (3) apply batching/quantization recommendations via Optimize.

Data sources & canonical queries (ops notes):
- Metrics store: metrics-prod (time-series). Canonical queries live in the metrics repo under /dashboards/qbr-canon.
- Billing: billing-warehouse (daily snapshots). Use the cost-sim job id in linked_artifacts for reproducibility.
- Cache telemetry: kv-cache-service logs + prefix-cache counters aggregated to metrics-prod.

Notes to self / open questions:
- How do we handle multi-tenant requests that span multiple models for the same customer? (proposed: attribute by primary route)
- Should the QBR cost metric include support and storage amortization? For now exclude; add a note column in the QBR tables if included for enterprise deals.
- Agree on a single canonical list of maintenance windows to exclude (engineering to publish).

Next steps (owner actions):
- eng-sre to publish canonical queries and dashboards -> target 2024-06-30 (Priya).
- billing to add a cost breakdown report for top 10 accounts -> 2024-06-20 (Noah).
- CS to trial the ops-weighted grade in 3 QBRs and report feedback -> 2024-Q3 (Maya).

Appendix — quick examples: 
- Quick latency calc: sample latencies (ms) [120, 130, 400, 410, 420, 1500] -> p50=410? (compute exact during cut&paste).
- Quick cost calc: runtime hours * GPU hourly cost / tokens processed (use cost-sim for bucketed accuracy).

(End of notebook draft)

-- Notes: this is intentionally informal; will convert to a clean QBR template once owners confirm canonical queries and targets.
